contract.scanner_units: Each scanner's Facts gains units: [{ file: rel posix, owners: [container key], project: project/package name, projectKind: csharp kind (web|worker|app|functions|library) or js kind (spa|api|library), root: rel dir of the project, or of the package's src/ when one exists, lang: 'C#'|'F#'|'TS'|'JS' }]. There is one unit per non-test source file under root. Files outside root are not units, such as vite.config.ts beside a package's src/. When pinning (component_edges a) meets such an evidence file, it maps to App shell, which is then created if absent. A library file's owners are the deployables whose closure includes it (csharp.js ownersOf :210 and owners :280; js-calls.js ownersOf :279). Test projects and TEST_RE files (js.js:9) produce no units. merge (index.js:28) concatenates units, and facts does not emit them.

contract.component_assignment: extract/components.js assigns each unit, per owner container, to exactly one component. Precedence: (1) designc.json extract.components override, first match wins. (2) C# anchors: a class with at least one [Function(...)] method, a class whose name ends in Controller or that derives from ControllerBase/Controller, or a static class calling Map(Get|Post|Put|Patch|Delete|Methods|Group). The component is named after the class and holds the class's file(s). (3) C# output-binding types: the T in Task<T>/ValueTask<T>/T returned by a [Function] method joins that method's class component, even when declared in another file of the same project. (4) A library project or package becomes one component named after the project/package inside each owner container. (5) Files directly in root become 'App shell'. (6) TS/JS support folders (types, constants, styles, assets, test, tests, mocks, __mocks__, case-insensitive) become 'Shared'. (7) A grouping folder (features, modules, domains, case-insensitive) as the first folder steps down one level: root/features/orders/** becomes 'orders', and files directly in root/features become 'features'. (8) Otherwise the first folder under root names the component. F# files use rules 4, 5 and 8 only. Anchor detection runs on csharp.js blanked code (blankComments), so commented-out classes do not count.
contract.component_ids: The component id (DSL identifier) is 'c_' + keyOf(container name) + '_' + keyOf(component name). keyOf (link.js:4) is [a-z0-9] only, so '_' is unambiguous. On a collision inside one container, suffix _2, _3 in component-name order. Components sort by name (localeCompare 'en') for deterministic output. A library component in two containers therefore has two ids.
contract.component_edges: facts.componentEdges: [{ from: component id, to: component id | element id ('e_' + keyOf(name)), kind: 'sync'|'async'|'data'|'realtime', label, tech, via: 'container-edge'|'queue-internal'|'type'|'di'|'di-candidate'|'import', evidence: [{file,line,text}] }]. The layers are built as follows. (a) Pinned container edges: for every facts.edges entry, each pair (or, if the edge has no pairs, each evidence item as the from-end with a null to-end) maps its from-end file to a component of edge.from. The to-end maps to a component of edge.to when the target is a deployable with pinnable evidence; to the element itself when the target is a store or external; and to the target container element itself when the target is a deployable and the to-end is null. Evidence files that are not source units (.csproj, designc.json, package.json, appsettings) map to the deepest project: a library maps to its library component, a deployable to App shell. http edges are relabelled 'Calls N endpoint(s)' with N = distinct pair.call values per component pair, and all other kinds keep the container label verbatim. (b) facts.internal queue links become async edges from each send's component to each receive's component, labelled 'Sends via "<key>"' with the link tech. (c) C# type and DI edges and (d) TS/JS import edges are intra-container, kind 'sync', label 'Uses', tech 'in-process', except DI candidates, which are labelled 'Uses (DI candidate)'. Same-component edges are dropped. Edges are de-duplicated by (from, to, kind) with evidence appended, and a certain edge absorbs a DI-candidate edge for the same pair. Rollup invariant: folding every componentEdge end to its container and dropping self-loops yields exactly the (from, to, kind) set of facts.edges.
contract.csharp_references: Type index: class, record, struct and interface declarations per project from blanked code, with namespace (reuse the span logic at csharp.js:283-286). A referencing file sees the declarations in its project's closure (csharp.js closure :186). A simple name resolves only if exactly one declaration in that closure has it; otherwise nothing happens. References are collected from: ctor and primary-ctor parameters, minimal-API lambda parameters, parameters of [Function] and controller action methods, field and property types, generic arguments of those, new T(, GetRequiredService<T> and GetService<T>. DI registrations are collected per deployable closure: (Try)?Add(Singleton|Scoped|Transient)<I, Impl>, the typeof(I), typeof(Impl) forms, AddHttpClient<I, Impl>, factory lambdas containing new Impl(, and single-type Add*<T>, which counts as a reference from the registering file to T. A reference to an interface I produces an edge to I's declaring component and, per registration Impl of I in that deployable, an edge to Impl's component. If I has more than one registration in the deployable, those implementation edges are 'di-candidate' and one unresolved entry { where: container, what: '<I> has N registrations (<Impl1>, <Impl2>); component edges to them are marked DI candidate', file, line, text } is added at the first registration.
contract.designc_json: "extract": { "bindings": { ... }, "components": [ { "name": "<component name>", "paths": ["<repo-relative posix glob>", ...] } ] }. extract/glob.js is a built-in matcher supporting **, * and ? (no braces or negation), case-sensitive, on repo-relative posix paths. A file matched in several containers becomes the named component in each. An entry without a string name or a non-empty paths array goes to unresolved (where 'designc.json'). A glob that matches no unit goes to unresolved: extract.components "<name>": "<glob>" matches no source file. main.js:189-192 already passes readSettings().extract as opts, so main.js does not change.
contract.dsl: dsl.render(repoName, elements, edges, components, componentEdges). With no components, the output is byte-identical to slice 1. A container with components renders as '      e_x = container "N" "" "T" {' followed by one line per component, '        c_x_y = component "Name" "" "tech"', then '      }'. All container-level relationships render exactly as today (5-line blocks, same order, dsl.js:13) and come first. Component relationships follow, each on ONE line: '    <from> -> <to> "label" "tech" { properties { "d.interaction" "sync|async" } }'. The one-line form is what Core.containerLevelText relies on. No new d.* properties are allowed (core.js:212 raises DC000 on unknown d.* keys), and relationship tags are not parsed (core.js:79-88), so the DI-candidate marker is carried by the label.
contract.core_atLevel: Core.atLevel(model, level), level in 'context'|'container'|'component', is pure and returns a new model built with makeModel (core.js:135). Every element deeper than the level folds into its nearest ancestor at or above that level. At 'context', containers fold into their softwareSystem and people and systems stay. Each rel maps its src and dst to their fold targets. Self-loops are dropped. A rel whose endpoints are both already at or above the level ('explicit') is kept. A lifted rel is dropped if an explicit rel with the same (src, dst) exists; otherwise the first lifted rel per (src, dst, description) is kept. Rel ids, lines and props are preserved, and errors are copied. Core.containerLevelText(text) returns the text with every component-declaration line and every relationship line whose src or dst is a component removed, located by parse line numbers. It assumes the one-line forms written by dsl.js and leaves everything else byte-identical. Both are exported next to the existing API (core.js:445).
